_doc: Organization stance claims extracted per t/1553 Stage 1. Feeds Stage 2/3 claim→node matching. Machine-proposed / human-disposes downstream.

claims.text: If current training paradigms remain unchanged, we should expect more capable models to develop even higher levels of situational awareness.
claims.canonical_proposition: Continued use of current training paradigms will lead to increased levels of situational awareness in more capable AI models.

claims.text: Addressing this likely requires tools that tell you about the model’s motivational structure, not just its inputs and outputs.
claims.canonical_proposition: Effective detection of AI scheming requires tools capable of assessing a model's internal motivational structure rather than relying solely on input-output analysis.

claims.text: we have no evidence that today’s deployed frontier models could suddenly “flip a switch” and begin engaging in significantly harmful scheming
claims.canonical_proposition: Current deployed frontier models do not possess the capability to spontaneously initiate significantly harmful scheming.

claims.text: we argued that chain-of-thought monitorability is promising but fragile and recommended that frontier developers avoid training practices that erode this key oversight signal.
claims.canonical_proposition: Frontier AI developers ought to avoid training practices that diminish the monitorability of chain-of-thought reasoning.

claims.text: we urge model developers to preserve reasoning transparency until better methods for studying and eliminating scheming have been developed.
claims.canonical_proposition: Model developers ought to maintain transparency of model reasoning processes until superior methods for mitigating AI scheming are developed.

claims.text: Scheming poses a real challenge for alignment, and addressing it must be a core part of AGI development.
claims.canonical_proposition: Developers must make addressing AI scheming a core component of AGI development.

claims.text: The framework allows users to zoom in on specific risks that are typical of AI, such as bias, explainability and robustness
claims.canonical_proposition: AI classification frameworks should enable the identification and analysis of specific AI risks, including bias, explainability, and robustness.

claims.text: The framework provides a baseline framework to help support and advance: Risk assessment, incident reporting and risk management
claims.canonical_proposition: The OECD AI classification framework ought to be used to support AI risk assessment, incident reporting, and risk management processes.

claims.text: The framework provides a baseline framework to help support and advance: Sector-specific frameworks, e.g. in healthcare
claims.canonical_proposition: The OECD AI classification framework ought to be used to support the development of sector-specific AI frameworks.

claims.text: The framework provides a baseline framework to help support and advance: Registries or inventories of AI systems
claims.canonical_proposition: The OECD AI classification framework ought to be used to support the creation of registries or inventories of AI systems.

claims.text: The framework provides a baseline framework to help support and advance: A common understanding of AI, and metrics
claims.canonical_proposition: The OECD AI classification framework ought to serve as a baseline to establish common understandings and metrics for AI systems.

claims.text: We’re now adding more detail about how we’ll design strong safeguards and verify their effectiveness in dedicated Safeguards Reports
claims.canonical_proposition: The organization produces Safeguards Reports to detail the design and verification of safety measures.

claims.text: We’ve built a growing suite of automated evaluations that can keep up with this faster cadence, while also continuing to do expert-led “deep dives”
claims.canonical_proposition: The organization utilizes both automated evaluations and expert-led deep dives to assess AI capabilities.

claims.text: Persuasion risks will be handled outside the Preparedness Framework
claims.canonical_proposition: The organization manages persuasion risks through mechanisms other than the Preparedness Framework.

claims.text: If another frontier AI developer releases a high-risk system without comparable safeguards, we may adjust our requirements.
claims.canonical_proposition: The organization may adjust its safety requirements if other frontier AI developers release high-risk systems without comparable safeguards.

claims.text: Systems that reach Critical capability also require safeguards that sufficiently minimize associated risks during development.
claims.canonical_proposition: Systems with Critical capability must have safeguards that sufficiently minimize severe harm risks during development.

claims.text: Covered systems that reach High capability must have safeguards that sufficiently minimize the associated risk of severe harm before they are deployed.
claims.canonical_proposition: Systems with High capability must have safeguards that sufficiently minimize severe harm risks before deployment.

claims.text: the risk should be plausible, measurable, severe, net new, and instantaneous or irremediable.
claims.canonical_proposition: An AI capability is a priority for preparedness if the risk is plausible, measurable, severe, net new, and instantaneous or irremediable.

claims.text: our RSP will not alter current uses of Claude or disrupt availability of our products.
claims.canonical_proposition: The organization ought not to disrupt the current availability or usage of Claude products through its Responsible Scaling Policy.

claims.text: Anthropic’s RSP has been formally approved by its board and changes must be approved by the board following consultations with the Long Term Benefit Trust
claims.canonical_proposition: The organization ought to require board approval and consultation with the Long Term Benefit Trust for any changes to its Responsible Scaling Policy.

claims.text: ASL-4 measures... may require methods of assurance that are unsolved research problems today, such as using interpretability methods to demonstrate mechanistically that a model is unlikely to engage in certain catastrophic behaviors.
claims.canonical_proposition: The organization ought to utilize mechanistic interpretability methods to demonstrate that models are unlikely to engage in catastrophic behaviors before deploying ASL-4 systems.

claims.text: a commitment not to deploy ASL-3 models if they show any meaningful catastrophic misuse risk under adversarial testing by world-class red-teamers
claims.canonical_proposition: The organization ought not to deploy ASL-3 models if they demonstrate meaningful catastrophic misuse risk during adversarial red-teaming.

claims.text: the ASL system implicitly requires us to temporarily pause training of more powerful models if our AI scaling outstrips our ability to comply with the necessary safety procedures.
claims.canonical_proposition: The organization ought to pause training of more powerful AI models if safety compliance capabilities are insufficient.

claims.text: The United States should instead allocate scarce resources toward approaches that will provide durable long-term advantages.
claims.canonical_proposition: The United States ought to allocate resources toward approaches providing durable long-term advantages rather than pursuing short-term AI first-mover advantages.

claims.text: The United States should begin investing now in mass and new capabilities for deception.
claims.canonical_proposition: The United States ought to increase investment in mass-produced systems and new deception capabilities.

claims.text: militaries must place deception and counter-reconnaissance at the center of how they operate to limit their losses.
claims.canonical_proposition: Militaries ought to prioritize deception and counter-reconnaissance to mitigate losses.

claims.text: Relying on small force structures of exquisite capabilities is quickly becoming a liability rather than an asset.
claims.canonical_proposition: Reliance on small force structures of exquisite capabilities is a liability.

claims.text: Mission commandùa hybrid of centralized and decentralized C2 modelsùwill remain desirable.
claims.canonical_proposition: Mission command remains the most desirable command and control paradigm despite AI advancements.

claims.text: Quantity could gain a significant edge over quality.
claims.canonical_proposition: Quantity of military assets will likely become more advantageous than quality in future warfare.

claims.text: The U.S. military might need to change important aspects of how it traditionally operates in order to exploit AIæs potential.
claims.canonical_proposition: The U.S. military ought to change its traditional operational methods to effectively exploit the potential of AI.

claims.text: National standards are necessary to maintain American leadership in AI.
claims.canonical_proposition: The United States must establish uniform national standards for artificial intelligence to maintain global leadership.

claims.text: A fragmented regulatory landscape creates uncertainty and hinders innovation.
claims.canonical_proposition: Fragmented state-level regulation of artificial intelligence creates market uncertainty and hinders technological innovation.

claims.text: The administration is eliminating state-level obstruction of national artificial intelligence policy.
claims.canonical_proposition: The federal government ought to preempt state-level artificial intelligence regulations to ensure a unified national policy framework.

claims.text: State-level AI regulations are an obstruction to national policy.
claims.canonical_proposition: State-level artificial intelligence regulations obstruct national policy.

claims.text: the statistical validity of LLM evaluations benefits from evaluators explicitly adopting a model for analyzing evaluation results
claims.canonical_proposition: Evaluators of large language models ought to explicitly adopt statistical models to analyze evaluation results to ensure validity.

claims.text: Building gold-standard AI systems requires gold-standard AI measurement science
claims.canonical_proposition: The development of high-quality AI systems requires the application of rigorous, gold-standard AI measurement science.

claims.text: collaborate with NIST staff to ensure U.S. dominance of international AI standards.
claims.canonical_proposition: The United States ought to maintain dominance in the development of international AI standards.

claims.text: Represent U.S. interests internationally to guard against burdensome and unnecessary regulation of American technologies by foreign governments
claims.canonical_proposition: Foreign governments ought not to impose burdensome and unnecessary regulations on American AI technologies.

claims.text: CAISI will focus on demonstrable risks, such as cybersecurity, biosecurity, and chemical weapons.
claims.canonical_proposition: CAISI ought to prioritize the evaluation of AI risks related to cybersecurity, biosecurity, and chemical weapons.

claims.text: CAISI will work with NIST staff to assist industry to develop voluntary standards.
claims.canonical_proposition: CAISI ought to assist the AI industry in developing voluntary standards.

claims.text: engaging history during futures exercises can expand the imagination of those engaged in backcasting and ground their discussion in historical realism.
claims.canonical_proposition: Integrating historical analysis into backcasting exercises improves the quality of futures planning by expanding imagination and grounding discussions in realism.

claims.text: the possibility of pursuing multilateral international cooperation to avoid the fragmentation of regulation and markets
claims.canonical_proposition: Policymakers ought to pursue multilateral international cooperation to prevent the fragmentation of AI regulations and markets.

claims.text: the need to enhance the government's ability to implement a more flexible regulatory system with more-effective collaboration among government and industry
claims.canonical_proposition: Governments ought to implement flexible regulatory systems characterized by effective collaboration between public and private sectors.

claims.text: developing more-sophisticated and more-nuanced AI governance models that strike a balance between encouraging innovation and ensuring the public good.
claims.canonical_proposition: Policymakers ought to develop AI governance models that balance innovation incentives with the protection of the public good.

claims.text: History can also help liberate the imagination.
claims.canonical_proposition: Historical analysis facilitates the expansion of imaginative capacity in futures planning.

claims.text: History can help inject realism into imagination by subjecting speculation about the future to lessons from the past.
claims.canonical_proposition: Incorporating historical analysis into futures exercises increases the realism of speculative scenarios.

claims.text: envisioning such utopias can prove useful if for no other reason than that the process can help identify near-term policies that are compatible with these many envisioned futures.
claims.canonical_proposition: Envisioning utopian futures is a useful method for identifying near-term policies that remain compatible across multiple potential future scenarios.

claims.text: Backcasting is valuable because it can help participants overcome the constraints that make it difficult to imagine a very different future and to consider near-term actions that might bring that future into being.
claims.canonical_proposition: Backcasting enables participants to overcome cognitive constraints regarding future scenarios and identify near-term actions to achieve desired outcomes.

claims.text: Building gold-standard AI systems requires gold-standard AI measurement science
claims.canonical_proposition: The development of high-quality AI systems requires the application of rigorous AI measurement science.

claims.text: Lead evaluations and assessments of potential security vulnerabilities and malign foreign influence arising from use of adversaries' AI systems
claims.canonical_proposition: CAISI ought to conduct evaluations of security vulnerabilities and malign foreign influence in adversary AI systems.

claims.text: collaborate with NIST staff to ensure U.S. dominance of international AI standards.
claims.canonical_proposition: CAISI ought to ensure U.S. dominance in the development of international AI standards.

claims.text: Represent U.S. interests internationally to guard against burdensome and unnecessary regulation of American technologies by foreign governments
claims.canonical_proposition: CAISI ought to oppose the implementation of burdensome and unnecessary foreign regulations on American AI technologies.

claims.text: CAISI will focus on demonstrable risks, such as cybersecurity, biosecurity, and chemical weapons.
claims.canonical_proposition: CAISI ought to prioritize the evaluation of cybersecurity, biosecurity, and chemical weapons risks in AI systems.

claims.text: CAISI will work with NIST staff to assist industry to develop voluntary standards.
claims.canonical_proposition: CAISI ought to assist industry in the development of voluntary AI standards.

claims.text: Maintain policies for training (and re-training) organizational staff about necessary legal or regulatory considerations that may impact AI-related design, development and deployment activities.
claims.canonical_proposition: Organizations ought to maintain training and retraining policies for staff regarding legal and regulatory considerations impacting AI activities.

claims.text: Align risk management efforts with applicable legal standards.
claims.canonical_proposition: Organizations ought to align their AI risk management efforts with applicable legal standards.

claims.text: Maintain awareness of the applicable legal and regulatory considerations and requirements specific to industry, sector, and business purpose, as well as the application context of the deployed AI system.
claims.canonical_proposition: Organizations ought to maintain awareness of legal and regulatory requirements specific to their industry, business purpose, and AI application context.

claims.text: All stakeholders benefit from policies, processes, and procedures which require preventing harm by design and default.
claims.canonical_proposition: Organizations ought to design and implement policies, processes, and procedures that prevent harm by design and default.

claims.text: Policies, processes, and procedures are central components of effective AI risk management and fundamental to individual and organizational accountability.
claims.canonical_proposition: Effective AI risk management and organizational accountability require the integration of policies, processes, and procedures.

claims.text: The Playbook is neither a checklist nor set of steps to be followed in its entirety. Playbook suggestions are voluntary.
claims.canonical_proposition: Organizations ought to treat the AI RMF Playbook suggestions as voluntary rather than mandatory requirements.

claims.text: All stakeholders benefit from policies, processes, and procedures which require preventing harm by design and default.
claims.canonical_proposition: Organizations ought to implement policies, processes, and procedures that require preventing harm by design and default.

claims.text: Align risk management efforts with applicable legal standards.
claims.canonical_proposition: Organizations ought to align their AI risk management efforts with applicable legal standards.

claims.text: Legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are understood, managed, and documented.
claims.canonical_proposition: Organizations ought to understand, manage, and document legal and regulatory requirements applicable to their AI systems.

claims.text: Organizations may utilize this information by borrowing as many – or as few – suggestions as apply to their industry use case or interests.
claims.canonical_proposition: Organizations ought to selectively implement AI RMF Playbook suggestions based on their specific industry use cases and interests.

claims.text: Playbook suggestions are voluntary.
claims.canonical_proposition: Adoption of the AI RMF Playbook suggestions is voluntary for organizations.

claims.text: The Playbook is neither a checklist nor set of steps to be followed in its entirety.
claims.canonical_proposition: Organizations ought not treat the AI RMF Playbook as a mandatory checklist or a comprehensive set of sequential steps.

claims.text: It may be more feasible for state governments to enact, and for industry and nongovernmental actors to adopt, some of the more promising measures.
claims.canonical_proposition: State governments, industry, and nongovernmental actors ought to enact or adopt promising measures to reduce catastrophic AI risks.

claims.text: Decisionmakers may be well-served by focusing on the more promising categories (such as those listed above), which may be implemented without federal government involvement.
claims.canonical_proposition: Decisionmakers ought to prioritize policy measures that can be implemented without federal government involvement.

claims.text: The likelihood of comprehensive measures being adopted by the federal government to reduce catastrophic AI risks in the near term (five to ten years) is perceived as low.
claims.canonical_proposition: The federal government is unlikely to adopt comprehensive measures to reduce catastrophic AI risks within the next five to ten years.

claims.text: Heavier-handed and stricter regulations, such as mandatory audits, government-imposed restrictions on actors, and mandatory safety standards, emerged as the least promising categories.
claims.canonical_proposition: Mandatory audits, government-imposed restrictions, and mandatory safety standards are the least promising policy categories for reducing the probability of catastrophic AI-caused harms.

claims.text: the most promising legal and policy categories to shape incentives for AI developers to reduce the probability of catastrophic AI-caused harms were incentives to find and disclose risks and voluntary safety standards.
claims.canonical_proposition: Incentives to find and disclose risks and voluntary safety standards are the most promising policy categories for reducing the probability of catastrophic AI-caused harms.

claims.text: NIST AI 800-3 argues that the statistical validity of LLM evaluations benefits from evaluators explicitly adopting a model for analyzing evaluation results
claims.canonical_proposition: Evaluators of LLMs ought to adopt explicit statistical models to analyze evaluation results.

claims.text: collaborate with NIST staff to ensure U.S. dominance of international AI standards.
claims.canonical_proposition: The U.S. ought to maintain dominance in the development of international AI standards.

claims.text: Represent U.S. interests internationally to guard against burdensome and unnecessary regulation of American technologies by foreign governments
claims.canonical_proposition: The U.S. government ought to prevent foreign governments from imposing burdensome and unnecessary regulations on American AI technologies.

claims.canonical_proposition: CAISI ought to prioritize the evaluation of AI risks related to cybersecurity, biosecurity, and chemical weapons.

claims.text: CAISI will work with NIST staff to assist industry to develop voluntary standards.
claims.canonical_proposition: CAISI ought to assist industry in the development of voluntary AI standards.

claims.canonical_proposition: Organizations ought to implement policies, processes, and procedures that mandate the prevention of harm by design and default.

claims.text: Policies, processes, and procedures are central components of effective AI risk management and fundamental to individual and organizational accountability.
claims.canonical_proposition: Effective AI risk management and accountability require the integration of policies, processes, and procedures.

claims.text: Organizations may utilize this information by borrowing as many – or as few – suggestions as apply to their industry use case or interests.
claims.canonical_proposition: Organizations ought to select only the AI RMF Playbook suggestions that are relevant to their specific industry use case or interests.

claims.canonical_proposition: Organizations are not required to follow the suggestions provided in the AI RMF Playbook.
